claim: Scam callers pose as CBI officers (also ED officials and judicial authorities) on phone and video calls
source_quote: The victims have alleged that they were contacted by persons impersonating CBI officers, ED officials and judicial authorities through telephone and video calls.
note: Primary: SC record of proceedings 17.10.2025, para 1. Also TNM 10 Mar 2026 (judge case): caller claimed to be a senior CBI officer (https://www.thenewsminute.com/telangana/hyderabad-retired-judge-loses-rs-166-crore-in-digital-arrest-scam-using-ex-cbi-officers-name). Hook line is a SIMULATION of this pattern.

claim: Typical opening: your Aadhaar is linked to a money-laundering case and there is an arrest warrant against you
source_quote: Aadhaar details were linked to a money-laundering and human trafficking case
note: Same report: 'a non-bailable arrest warrant had been issued against him'. Same pattern elsewhere: Deccan Herald 22 Dec 2024, a fake officer 'accused her of money laundering' (https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnataka/bengaluru/under-digital-arrest-for-11-days-housewife-breaks-3-fds-to-pay-fraudsters-rs-30-lakh-3328890).

claim: Victims are told not to go anywhere, not to tell anyone and to stay on camera
source_quote: The scammers warned the former judge not to step out of his house
note: Newsmeter 9 Mar 2026 also: 'They also instructed him not to discuss the matter with family members or friends.' and 'kept him under virtual surveillance through video calls.' MHA alert 14 May 2024: victims 'remain visually available over Skype or other video conferencing platforms' (https://www.etvbharat.com/en/!bharat/ministry-of-home-affairs-issues-nationwide-alert-over-digital-arrest-enn24051405886).

claim: Lifetime savings vanish 'in a few hours, a few days at most' (te: కొన్ని గంటల్లో, మహా అయితే కొన్ని రోజుల్లో)
source_quote: defrauded of their life savings through a “digital arrest” scam perpetrated between 03.09.2025 and 16.09.2025
note: Documented cases last far longer than 'a few days at most': Haryana couple 3-16 Sep 2025 (SC order); Hebbal engineer 'over an 18-day period' (TNM 23 Dec 2024, https://www.thenewsminute.com/karnataka/bengaluru-software-engineer-loses-rs-118-crore-in-digital-arrest-scam); Mumbai businessman Rs 58.13 crore 'over 40 days' (AIR 17 Oct 2025, https://www.newsonair.gov.in/digital-arrest-scam); Bengaluru engineer about Rs 32 crore, 'the ordeal lasted for over six months' (PTI/DT Next 17 Nov 2025, https://www.dtnext.in/news/national/bengaluru-woman-loses-rs-3183-cr-in-months-long-digital-arrest-scam-involving-fake-cbi-officers-853424). 'Hours' is sourced: Mangaluru, call at 10 am, Rs 17 lakh sent around 3 pm the same day (Deccan Herald 31 Oct 2025, https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnataka/mangaluru/mangaluru-police-recover-rs-17-lakh-duped-in-digital-arrest-3781567). REPLACEMENT te: జీవితమంతా కష్టపడి దాచుకున్న డబ్బు, కొన్ని రోజుల్లో, కొన్నిసార్లు కొన్ని గంటల్లోనే, మాయం. en: Money saved over a whole lifetime, gone in a few days, sometimes in just a few hours.

claim: The Supreme Court does not send warrants over the phone
source_quote: Every warrant of arrest issued by a Court under this Sanhita shall be in writing, signed by the presiding officer of such Court and shall bear the seal of the Court.
note: BNSS 2023 s.72(1) (Gazette text). s.74(1): 'A warrant of arrest shall ordinarily be directed to one or more police officers'. s.227 proviso lets a Magistrate issue summons or warrants 'through electronic means', but a warrant still goes to police for execution, not to the accused by phone. The SC's own order of 17.10.2025 calls the WhatsApp/video 'orders' forgeries (https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2025/59769/59769_2025_2_7_65003_Order_17-Oct-2025.pdf).

note: TNM: 'Ironically, retired IPS officer Archana Ramasundaram was with the CBI and scamsters are known to imitate real people'. The Better India 2 Feb 2016: 'a Tamil Nadu cadre IPS officer', DG of SSB 'till the date of her superannuation on September 30, 2017' (https://www.thebetterindia.com/44776/archana-ramasundram-paramilitary-force-head/). VO unchanged: ఆయన మల్కాజ్గిరి సైబర్ క్రైమ్ పోలీసులకు కంప్లైంట్ ఇచ్చారు. en (unchanged): He complained to the Malkajgiri cyber crime police.

MHA alert 14 May 2024 lists police, CBI, NCB and RBI impersonation (https://www.sentinelassam.com/more-news/national-news/mha-alerts-against-blackmail-digital-arrest-by-cyber-criminals-posing-government-agency-officers). claim: Stories used: drugs in a parcel in your name, a crime committed with your SIM, laundered money in your account
source_quote: parcel, which contains illegal goods, drugs, fake passports or any other contraband item
note: MHA alert, Sentinel Assam 15 May 2024. Deccan Herald 22 Dec 2024: 'a SIM card purchased in Mumbai in her name was used to send harassment messages' and a fake officer 'accused her of money laundering' (https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnataka/bengaluru/under-digital-arrest-for-11-days-housewife-breaks-3-fds-to-pay-fraudsters-rs-30-lakh-3328890); PTI 17 Nov 2025: parcel 'contained credit cards, passports and MDMA'.

claim: They move the victim to a video call on WhatsApp or Skype
source_quote: The fraudsters displayed forged orders of the Supreme Court through WhatsApp and video conferencing.
note: MHA alert 14 May 2024: victims 'remain visually available over Skype or other video conferencing platforms' (https://www.etvbharat.com/en/!bharat/ministry-of-home-affairs-issues-nationwide-alert-over-digital-arrest-enn24051405886); the I4C Oct 2024 advisory showed the WhatsApp and Skype logos (https://www.etvbharat.com/en/!bharat/cbi-ed-police-dont-arrest-people-through-video-calls-indian-cyber-crime-coordination-centre-enn24100602996); the Oswal hearing was on Skype.

claim: MHA said the gangs use studios modelled on police stations and government offices and wear uniforms (on-screen: [MHA / I4C ALERT | MAY 2024])
source_quote: studios modelled on police stations and government offices and wear uniforms

The alert was issued on Tuesday 14 May 2024. Tag correct.

claim: Some victims are even shown a fake court hearing
source_quote: staged a fake virtual courtroom
note: Bar & Bench 1 Oct 2024 (Oswal case). Mangaluru, Oct 2025: a WhatsApp video call 'impersonating police officers and a judge' (Deccan Herald 31 Oct 2025, https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnataka/mangaluru/mangaluru-police-recover-rs-17-lakh-duped-in-digital-arrest-3781567).

source_quote: a person impersonating Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud
note: TNM 2 Oct 2024: the fake judge was introduced as 'CJI Chandrachud' (https://thenewsminute.com/news/how-an-indian-ceo-lost-rs-7-crore-to-scammers-who-pretended-to-be-ed-cbi-and-cji); Bar & Bench 1 Oct 2024. The VO does not name him and the visual uses no CJI photo (keep it that way).

claim: On-screen: ₹7 CRORE · SEPT 2024 [BAR & BENCH | BUSINESS STANDARD]
source_quote: The scam unfolded on August 28 and 29
note: The fraud took place 28-30 Aug 2024 (Business Standard; TNM: 28-30 Aug; Moneylife: 29-30 Aug) and the complaint was filed on 31 Aug 2024. claim: A stamped order then arrived on WhatsApp
source_quote: During a video call, the industrialist was shown a fake court order, which he later received via WhatsApp
note: Sentinel Assam 30 Sep 2024: 'They later WhatsApped Oswal, with the forged order of the court.' (https://www.sentinelassam.com/cities/guwahati-city/guwahati-duo-arrested-in-rs-7-crore-scam-targeting-industrialist-sp-oswal); TNM: 'The written SC order was so perfect and stamped that I believed it to be genuine'.

source_quote: sent a fake Supreme Court order directing him to send ₹7 crore to a Secret Supervision Account
note: Business Standard: 'was defrauded of Rs 7 crore'. Police later recovered Rs 5.25 crore (Business Standard: 'leading to the recovery of Rs 5.25 crore'); the VO does not say otherwise.

claim: A Haryana elderly couple were shown forged Supreme Court orders and lost about Rs 1.05 crore; their case started the SC suo motu case (on-screen: ₹1.05 CR · SUO MOTU, OCT 2025 [SUPREME COURT OF INDIA])
source_quote: The instant suo motu writ petition has arisen out of a complaint dated 21.09.2025 received by this Court from a senior citizen couple

REPLACEMENT te: హర్యానా లో ఒక వృద్ధ దంపతులకి, సుప్రీం కోర్ట్ పేరుతో, జడ్జి ల సంతకాలు ఫోర్జ్ చేసిన ఆర్డర్స్ చూపించి, వన్ క్రోర్ ఫైవ్ లాక్స్ కి పైగా కొట్టేశారు. ఆ కేస్ తోనే సుప్రీం కోర్ట్ ఈ స్కామ్ ని సుమోటో గా తీసుకుంది. en: In Haryana, an elderly couple was shown orders in the Supreme Court's name with judges' forged signatures, and robbed of over one crore five lakh. That case is what made the Supreme Court take up this scam on its own.

claim: Oswal was told to keep Skype on even while he slept (on-screen REC timer 47:12:09)
source_quote: they instructed me to keep the Skype in my phone on even during sleep
note: Moneylife 30 Sep 2024; TNM 2 Oct 2024 carries the same quote (https://thenewsminute.com/news/how-an-indian-ceo-lost-rs-7-crore-to-scammers-who-pretended-to-be-ed-cbi-and-cji). The stylised 47-hour REC timer is consistent with Business Standard: the scam 'left Oswal under "digital arrest" for two days'.

claim: One call to a family member or friend quickly exposes the scam (why they forbid telling family)
source_quote: Later that evening, around 6 pm, she confided in a neighbour, who immediately took her to the CEN police station at 7 pm
note: Police froze the full Rs 17 lakh that evening (Deccan Herald 31 Oct 2025). Oswal also realised it was a scam after confiding in a senior colleague (Business Standard 1 Oct 2024). 'Within minutes' is the narrator's emphasis, not a measured figure (optional softening in fact-check.md).

claim: In Hyderabad a 76-year-old retired doctor was kept in digital arrest for about 70 hours and later died of a heart attack (on-screen: 70 HOURS [MEDICAL DIALOGUES | SEPT 2025])
source_quote: suffered a heart attack after being kept under 'digital arrest' for nearly 70 hours
note: Medical Dialogues 29 Sep 2025. Siasat 17 Sep 2025: '70-hour digital arrest by fraudsters', death 'on September 8 by cardiac arrest', police case 'including charges of culpable homicide not amounting to murder' after the family's complaint (https://www.siasat.com/hyderabad-retired-doctor-dies-after-rs-6-6l-cyber-fraud-digital-arrest-3272364/). The Logical Indian 18 Sep 2025: 'a fatal heart attack on September 8' (https://thelogicalindian.com/hyderabad-retired-doctor-dies-of-heart-attack-after-70-hour-digital-arrest-scam-duped-of-%e2%82%b96-6-lakh/). Reports say heart attack or cardiac arrest; the link to the scam rests on the family's complaint and the police charge. Not a suicide, so Press Council suicide norms do not apply.

claim: They demand the money be sent to a 'safe account' for verification and call it an 'RBI account' (on-screen: SIMULATION · FAKE ACCOUNT)
source_quote: The caller threatened that she would be arrested unless she deposited her money into a Reserve Bank of India (RBI) account for “verification.”
note: Deccan Herald 31 Oct 2025, from Mangaluru DCP Mithun H N. TNM 23 Dec 2024: 'the fraudsters presented a fake Reserve Bank of India guideline document and demanded that the victim transfer money for verification purposes.' (https://www.thenewsminute.com/karnataka/bengaluru-software-engineer-loses-rs-118-crore-in-digital-arrest-scam).

claim: They also call it a 'secret supervision account'
source_quote: directed to release all my funds to into a secret supervision account.
note: Oswal's statement (LiveLaw 1 Oct 2024). Bar & Bench: 'a fake Supreme Court order directing him to send ₹7 crore to a Secret Supervision Account.' (https://barandbench.com/news/fraudsters-pose-as-cji-fake-virtual-courtroom-dupe-industrialist).

claim: (implied) The RBI does not keep accounts for individuals, so an 'RBI account' is fake
source_quote: RBI does not hold any accounts for individuals.
note: RBI press release 4 Jul 2018; the same sentence is in RBI's release of 6 Feb 2012 (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=25911).

claim: They promise everything comes back after verification
source_quote: I was told that money will be returned by February 25 after completion of all procedures,
note: Bengaluru engineer (PTI/DT Next 17 Nov 2025). Judge case: Newsmeter, 'would be refunded'.

source_quote: On December 4, 5 and 7, Lavina broke FDs worth Rs 10 lakh, Rs 9 lakh and Rs 8.5 lakh, respectively, and transferred them to the fraudsters based on their insistence.
note: ETV Bharat 12 Nov 2025: 'forced to liquidate 18 FDs for the payment.' (https://www.etvbharat.com/en/state/ajmer-retired-bank-employee-loses-rs-8-dot67-lakh-to-digital-arrest-scam-enn25111204618); Deccan Herald 31 Oct 2025 (Mangaluru): told to 'liquidate her fixed deposits and savings'.

claim: The money moves through layer after layer of mule accounts in other people's names, and out (on-screen: MULE ACCOUNTS)
source_quote: the masterminds behind the scam used over 6,500 fake bank accounts, spread across 13 layers, to launder the stolen money.
note: AIR/newsonair 17 Oct 2025 (Maharashtra Cyber). SC order 04.08.2026: CBI identified '67 first-layer bank accounts' (https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2025/59769/59769_2025_1_30_72575_Order_04-Aug-2026.pdf); RBI via FPJ 7 Aug 2026: 'A money mule is a person who receives or transfers illegally obtained money for someone else.' (https://www.freepressjournal.in/business/easy-money-offer-could-be-a-trap-rbi-warns-against-becoming-a-money-mule); MHA official (ThePrint): 'The second vertical moves the money into mule accounts.'

claim: Officials say many (te: చాలావరకు, i.e. most) of these calls come from scam centres in countries like Cambodia, Myanmar and Thailand (on-screen: [MHA OFFICIALS | THEPRINT, FEB 2026])
source_quote: Many of these scam calls were traced to networks operating out of Thailand, Cambodia, and Myanmar.
note: Senior MHA official to ThePrint (18 Feb 2026). ThePrint also: 'According to another source, most digital arrest calls originate from "scam farms" operating out of Thailand and Cambodia.' I4C CEO (Outlook 23 May 2024): '45 per cent of cyber financial frauds taking place in the country are originating from the South East Asia' (names Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos) (https://www.outlookindia.com/amp/story/national/spurt-in-cybercrimes-in-india-carried-out-by-organised-gangs-based-in-south-east-asia-govt). RECOMMENDED: te చాలావరకు (mostly) -> చాలా (many), to match the official's words and the en column.

claim: Once the money is gone, getting it back is very hard
source_quote: In 2021, only 6 percent of the defrauded money was blocked.
note: ThePrint: 'By 2026, that figure had risen to 19 percent'. SC order 04.08.2026: 'restoration completed in 36,290 cases for an aggregate amount of Rs. 18.05 crores'; SC order 01.12.2025: the crimes are 'often beyond the territorial jurisdiction of India' (https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2025/59769/59769_2025_1_28_66412_Order_01-Dec-2025.pdf). Exception worth knowing: police recovered Rs 5.25 crore of Oswal's Rs 7 crore.

claim: 'Digital arrest' does not exist in Indian law (on-screen: DIGITAL ARREST — NOT IN LAW [BNSS 2023 | MHA / I4C])
source_quote: In fact, the recently enacted new criminal law does not provide for any legal provisions of conducting digital arrest.
note: Rajasthan High Court (Justice Anoop Kumar Dhand), Verdictum 24 Jan 2025. BNSS 2023 Gazette text has no such provision; an arrest needs physical touch or confinement (s.43) (https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/250884_2_english_01042024.pdf). Mangaluru DCP (Deccan Herald 31 Oct 2025): 'There is no such legal process as a ‘digital arrest’ in India.' Tag: no MHA/I4C source found saying 'not in law' (I4C said agencies don't arrest on video calls). RECOMMENDED tag: [BNSS 2023 | RAJASTHAN HIGH COURT, JAN 2025].

claim: PM Modi said in Mann Ki Baat (27 Oct 2024) there is no system like digital arrest in the law; it is fraud (on-screen: [MANN KI BAAT | 27 OCT 2024])
source_quote: There is no system like digital arrest in the law, this is just fraud, deceit, lie,
note: Odisha Bytes 27 Oct 2024: 'there is no system like digital arrest in the law' (https://odishabytes.com/pm-modi-flags-digital-arrest-in-mann-ki-baat-spells-mantra-to-combat-cybercrimes/amp/); 115th episode. The Telugu line is a faithful condensed translation (paraphrase) of the English rendering.

claim: I4C advisory (Oct 2024): CBI, police, customs, ED and judges do not arrest anyone on a video call (on-screen: NO ARREST ON VIDEO CALL [I4C ADVISORY | OCT 2024])
source_quote: Don't Panic, Stay Alert. CBI/Police/Custom/ED/Judges DO NOT arrest you on video call.
note: Issued Saturday 5 Oct 2024, PTI report 6 Oct 2024 (also Tribune, Deccan Herald). Tag correct.

claim: The BNSS is India's new criminal procedure law (on-screen: BNSS 2023 · BHARATIYA NAGARIK SURAKSHA SANHITA)
source_quote: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Criminal Procedure.
note: Act No. 46 of 2023, President's assent 25 Dec 2023 (Gazette of India Extraordinary).

claim: BNSS s.43: an arrest needs the officer to actually touch or confine you, or your submission to custody (on-screen: 1 · PHYSICAL ARREST [BNSS S.43])
source_quote: In making an arrest the police officer or other person making the same shall actually touch or confine the body of the person to be arrested, unless there be a submission to the custody by word or action
note: s.43(1). Proviso: for a woman, submission is presumed on oral intimation and a male officer shall not touch her; it is still an in-person arrest. No change needed.

claim: BNSS s.36(a): the arresting officer's name must be clearly visible (name badge) (on-screen: 2 · NAME VISIBLE [BNSS S.36])
source_quote: bear an accurate, visible and clear identification of his name which will facilitate easy identification
note: D.K. Basu's wording was 'name tags', so 'name badge' is apt.

claim: BNSS s.36(b): an arrest memo attested by a family member or a respectable local, and signed by you too (on-screen: 3 · ARREST MEMO + WITNESS [BNSS S.36])
source_quote: attested by at least one witness, who is a member of the family of the person arrested or a respectable member of the locality where the arrest is made
note: s.36(b)(ii): 'countersigned by the person arrested'. 'Locality where the arrest is made' equals 'your area' when you are arrested at home.

claim: BNSS s.48: your relatives or a friend must be told at once of the arrest and where you are held (on-screen: 4 · FAMILY INFORMED [BNSS S.48])
source_quote: forthwith give the information regarding such arrest and place where the arrested person is being held to any of his relatives, friends or such other persons as may be disclosed or nominated by the arrested person

claim: BNSS s.58: you must be taken before a magistrate within 24 hours (on-screen: 5 · MAGISTRATE IN 24 H [BNSS S.58])
source_quote: such period shall not, in the absence of a special order of a Magistrate under section 187, exceed twenty-four hours exclusive of the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the Magistrate's Court
note: s.58 covers arrest without warrant; the s.78 proviso gives the same 24 hours for arrests under a warrant; Constitution Art. 22(2) (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/581566/). Journey time is excluded; no change needed.

claim: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal (1996) is the source of the name-tag, arrest-memo and inform-a-relative rules, now in the BNSS (on-screen: [D.K. BASU v. STATE OF WEST BENGAL | 1996])
source_quote: should bear accurate, visible and clear identification and name togs with their designations.
note: Judgment of 18 Dec 1996 (Kuldip Singh and A.S. Anand JJ.), reported (1997) 1 SCC 416; 'togs' is the source's typo. Its requirements (1) to (3) (name tags; memo attested by a family member or respectable local and countersigned; right to have a friend or relative informed) match BNSS s.36 and s.48 (PIB comparison: '(S. 50A CrPC, now S. 48 BNSS)', https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2024/may/doc2024522337501.pdf). Tag year correct.

claim: All of 'these rules' (all five) rest on the D.K. Basu judgment (te: ఈ రూల్స్ కి పునాది)
source_quote: (S. 46 CrPC, now S. 43 BNSS)
note: Rule 1 (touch or confine, s.43) is the old CrPC s.46 rule, and rule 5 (24 hours, s.58) is CrPC s.57 and Constitution Art. 22(2) (same PIB document: '(S. 57 CrPC, now S. 58 BNSS)'). D.K. Basu's 11 requirements cover rules 2 to 4 only. REPLACEMENT te: నేమ్ బ్యాడ్జ్, అరెస్ట్ మెమో, ఫ్యామిలీ కి చెప్పడం, ఈ రూల్స్ సుప్రీం కోర్ట్ ఇచ్చిన డి కె బసు జడ్జిమెంట్ నుంచి వచ్చాయి. ఇప్పుడు అవి చట్టంలోనే ఉన్నాయి. en: The name badge, the arrest memo, telling your family: these rules came from the Supreme Court's D K Basu judgment. Today they are written into the law itself. Optional extra sentence te: ట్వెంటీ ఫోర్ అవర్స్ రూల్ అయితే మన రాజ్యాంగంలోనే ఉంది. en: And the twenty-four-hour rule is in our Constitution itself (Art. 22(2)).

claim: The law says your family must be told; the scammer says hide it from your family (on-screen: LAW: TELL FAMILY · SCAM: HIDE FROM FAMILY)
source_quote: to any of his relatives, friends or such other persons as may be disclosed or nominated by the arrested person
note: BNSS s.48(1). Scam side: TNM, the judge was 'warned ... not to disclose the matter to anyone, including my family'.

claim: No police, no court and not even the RBI will ask you to transfer money for verification
source_quote: No agency — including the police, judiciary, CBI, or ED — ever demands money transfers or deposits under such a pretext,
note: Mangaluru DCP Mithun H N (Deccan Herald 31 Oct 2025). RBI 6 Feb 2012: it 'never contacts the public via unsolicited phone calls or emails asking for money' (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=25911); RBI 4 Jul 2018: 'RBI does not hold any accounts for individuals.' (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=44392).

claim: On-screen tag: MONEY DEMAND = SCAM [RBI · I4C ADVISORIES]
source_quote: Don't Panic, Stay Alert. CBI/Police/Custom/ED/Judges DO NOT arrest you on video call.
note: The only I4C advisory found (Oct 2024) is about arrests on video calls; no I4C statement about money demands was found, so the I4C part of the tag is unsupported. REPLACEMENT on-screen: MONEY DEMAND = SCAM [RBI · POLICE ADVISORIES]. VO unchanged: ఇంకో విషయం. ఏ పోలీస్ గానీ, ఏ కోర్ట్ గానీ, ఆర్ బి ఐ గానీ, వెరిఫికేషన్ కోసం మీ డబ్బు ట్రాన్స్ఫర్ చేయమని అడగరు. డబ్బు అడిగారు అంటే, అది హండ్రెడ్ పర్సెంట్ స్కామ్. en (unchanged): One more thing. No police, no court, not even the RBI, will ask you to transfer your money for verification. If they asked for money, it's a hundred percent scam.

claim: A real case comes with a written notice you can verify at a police station
source_quote: The police officer shall, in all cases where the arrest of a person is not required under sub-section (1) issue a notice directing the person
note: BNSS s.35(3). The Supreme Court (Satender Kumar Antil v. CBI, 16 Jul 2025) held that s.35 notices cannot be served by WhatsApp or other electronic modes (https://www.scconline.com/blog/post/2025/07/31/supreme-court-section-35-bnss-notices-physical-service-mandate/). BNSS s.63 and s.64(2) do allow court summons by electronic communication, but only bearing the court seal image or a digital signature: still a written, checkable document, so the line holds. Police may arrest without prior notice in some cases (s.35(1)), but then in person with a memo (s.36).

claim: The number they give you to 'verify' leads to their own people
source_quote: The accused and the victim were then joined by another person on the call who claimed to be Circle Inspector Gourav Saradhi.
note: Deccan Herald 22 Dec 2024: the victim's call was 'transferred to the Pant Nagar police station in Mumbai' (a fake station). Advice line; no change.

source_quote: new modus operandi to commit fraud in digital payment ecosystem using remote screen access apps
note: NPCI warning reported 19 Feb 2019, following RBI Alert 1/2019 of 14 Feb 2019 on AnyDesk-type apps. Mangaluru DCP (Deccan Herald 31 Oct 2025): 'download only trusted apps'.

claim: 1930 is the national cybercrime helpline (on-screen: CALL 1930)
source_quote: report the incident on cybercrime helpline number 1930 or www.cybercrime.gov.in for assistance
note: MHA alert, 14 May 2024. I4C advisory Oct 2024: 'central helpline number 1930' (https://www.etvbharat.com/en/!bharat/cbi-ed-police-dont-arrest-people-through-video-calls-indian-cyber-crime-coordination-centre-enn24100602996); PM in Mann Ki Baat: dial 1930 to reach the national cyber helpline. Calling your bank at once is standard advice.

claim: File a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in (on-screen: cybercrime.gov.in)
source_quote: report the incident on cybercrime helpline number 1930 or www.cybercrime.gov.in for assistance
note: The site is the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (the SC order of 04.08.2026 calls it the 'National Cybercrime Reporting Portal').
